research_mode: official ONS and Home Office sources only; outcome cohort and closed-period semantics, timeliness and Crimsec4 limits, open-data schema and revision states, geography editions and current outcome snapshots; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: Crime outcomes technical annex: recorded-offence cohort method
verified_claims: the recorded-offence cohort method follows offences recorded in a defined reporting period
outcomes are linked back to individual recorded crimes
the distribution changes as investigations receive outcomes over time
limitations: recent cohorts are incomplete
cohort percentages require an extraction date

sources.name: Crime outcomes technical annex: investigations closed in period
verified_claims: the closed-period measure counts outcomes recorded in the reporting year
associated crimes may have been recorded in earlier years
the measure describes police activity across mixed crime cohorts
limitations: closed-period volumes are not a same-cohort resolution rate
crime-recording dates must remain separate

sources.name: Illustrative closed-period outcome-rate boundary
verified_claims: closed-period outcome rates can exceed 100 percent for some low-volume crimes
the technical annex calls these rates illustrative rather than true rates
the numerator can include outcomes for offences recorded in previous years
limitations: rates above 100 percent are not impossible values to clip
the measure must not be interpreted as a probability

sources.name: Closed-period rate crime-volume sensitivity
verified_claims: closed-period rates compare outcomes recorded in a year with crimes recorded in the same year
the two groups are not necessarily the same offences
changes in recorded-crime volumes can change the illustrative rate
limitations: volume-driven movement is not necessarily investigative-performance change
cross-period comparisons need cohort context

sources.name: Crime-outcome timeliness interpretation
verified_claims: timeliness measures elapsed time between offence recording and outcome assignment
it can be used as a proxy for investigative efficiency
the Home Office says it should not be considered a firm measure
limitations: administrative timing affects the measure
timeliness is not a parcel safety score

sources.name: Outcome action and system-recording delay
verified_claims: an outcome can be achieved before it is entered on the crime-recording system
recording delay affects measured timeliness
the technical annex distinguishes operational action from system implementation
limitations: system timestamps do not always equal operational decision time
force processes may differ

sources.name: Short-duration outcome administrative-lag example
verified_claims: some outcomes measured as taking one to five days may have been actioned on the offence date
cannabis-warning administration is given as an example
later system assignment can create apparent elapsed days
limitations: the example does not apply to every outcome
short elapsed time is not proof of same-day action

sources.name: Crimsec4 aggregated-return scope
verified_claims: a small number of forces submit monthly aggregated crime and outcome data using Crimsec4
the return is organised by notifiable offence
Crimsec4 differs from record-level Home Office Data Hub data
limitations: aggregated returns cannot support record-level linkage
force coverage can change by edition

sources.name: Crimsec4 outcome-application month
verified_claims: Crimsec4 records an outcome in the month it is applied
the original offence can have occurred months earlier
outcome data for a month may not correspond to offences in that month or year
limitations: application month must not be treated as offence month
aggregated monthly data cannot reconstruct exact case timelines

sources.name: Notifiable-offence-list scope
verified_claims: Crimsec4 covers offences in the notifiable offence list
the list includes offences that could be tried by jury
it also includes some closely related summary offences
limitations: notifiable crime is not all offending or all incidents
scope changes require offence-reference versioning
